description: Assembly track (assembly, assembly_call, cohort_pangenome) with the requests for the per-sample and chr20 scaling pilots, from the cluster smoke of 2026-10-22 on chr20-only assemblies. PAV: its two align_map jobs each hold minimap2's index of the whole reference (about 16 GB each, whatever the assembly's size) and peaked at 29 of 40 GB on chr20, so 120 GB and 16 cores (align_map on 8 threads per haplotype): three PAVs share a 48-core node and the pilot cannot be killed for memory. dipcall peaked at 32 of 48 GB on chr20: 64 GB. The pangenome's mapping (0.22.0): one task per member maps its two haplotypes to the reference-only graph, one after the other, on 8 cores (minigraph uses few cores of one mapping: 22 % CPU efficiency on five whole genomes) with 60 GB plus 15 times the member's gzipped FASTAs, about 85 GB for a whole genome; the split task that follows only partitions the gathered alignments and keeps its defaults (16 cores, 64 GB). The stage inputs below are the per-sample ones; the pangenome needs none on standard nodes. The chromosome task keeps its declared floor until the ladder has run. hifiasm keeps its 48 cores and 288 GiB, a whole standard node, which is why max_inflight is 10. Partition and time limits are rows of the site's resources.tsv (the worked policy of chapter 12 has them). For the ladder set stage_inputs.cohort_pangenome.chromosomes to ["chr20"] on the project. Replace these values with the measurements (ugc-wgw usage --by task).
